item.title: Distinguishing Process Change, Instrument Fault and Data-Path Corruption in Streaming Telemetry: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark
item.description: arXiv:2610.18904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A reading departs from what a monitoring system expects for one of three reasons: the physical process changed, the instrument is failing, or the value was corrupted between the instrument and the software. The three call for different responses and look alike in a single sample. We state the three-cause problem, prove which pairs of causes one channel cannot separate, and propose a bank of online detectors - a Kalman tracker with CUSUM and EWMA charts on its innovation, a Hampel median with generalized-ESD confirmation, a robust noise statistic with ADWIN, exact-value checks and an optional two-channel complementary filter - combined by a deterministic, inspectable attribution rule. The detectors were merged into a public algorithm library. On 2,942 injected events of thirteen fault types the method detects 96.3% (95% interval 95.7-97.0) at 0.22 false alarms per hour and attributes 91.2% (90.6-91.8) of detected events correctly from one channel and 99.0% (98.6-99.4) with a second, rate channel; from one channel only 2 of 207 detected sensor drifts are attributed to the instrument, as the problem statement predicts. Injected into recorded industrial signals, the same catalogue is detected at 80.8% and attributed correctly at 84.5%, at 3.6 false alarms per hour. On the Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark the method detects 32 of 33 experiments with a median delay of 15 s, at 46 false alarms per hour against 11 for a rolling z-score.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandr Klymenko

item.title: A Wideband STAR-RIS Employing Shared-Aperture Polarization Conversion and Diagonal Switching Topology for 6G Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.19040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (STAR-RIS) enable programmable wave control on both sides of a surface, extending wireless coverage beyond single-sided operation. However, practical STAR-RIS demonstrations in literature have narrow bandwidths, because it is challenging to achieve wideband reflection and transmission simultaneously from the same aperture. To overcome this limitation, a wideband STAR-RIS architecture is proposed based on shared-aperture polarization conversion and diagonal switching topology. Here, multiple resonances enable wideband magnitude responses and mirror-symmetric current reversal maintains $180^{\circ}$ phase difference in both reflection and transmission modes. Accordingly, a diagonal four-branch unit cell configuration is developed, where the tailored top patch directs the received wave either through a pair of blind vias connected by a buried strip to the shared top aperture for reflection, or to the bottom ring patch using a through via for transmission. Based on the proposed design, a 10 by 10 STAR-RIS prototype is fabricated and experimentally characterized. The measured 3-dB bandwidths reach 19.8% in reflection mode and 21.9% in transmission mode. Near-field measurements show average signal enhancements of 19.8 and 22.6 dB for reflection and transmission, respectively, over the wide frequency range of 6.8-8.4 GHz. Far-field measurements further demonstrate average received-power enhancements of 11.2 dB in reflection and 11.9 dB in transmission. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this work presents the first experimentally demonstrated wideband STAR-RIS covering the 7.125-8.4 GHz band within the emerging 6G FR3 spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Ruiqi Wang, Atif Shamim

item.title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment
item.description: arXiv:2610.19115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. The same test rejects unknown transmitters when scored against all enrolled vessels, and exposes insider spoofs when scored against the claimed vessel. A threshold refreshed from genuine traffic alone keeps it at a stated false-alarm rate as fingerprints drift. On AIS in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) recordings captured over 13 days at the Istanbul Strait (Bosphorus), the detector rejects unseen vessels at least 10 days after enrollment. Evaluated over 50-burst trials with every vessel weighted equally, it reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.956 (95% confidence interval 0.913-0.989), where the best score computed from one burst at a time reaches 0.899. A threshold refreshed from the first quarter of the enrolled vessels' traffic holds 5.3% false alarms (3.0-9.2% across five independently trained encoders) at 88.8% detection. Scored against the claimed MMSI, enrolled transmitters spoofing another vessel are rejected at 0.991, a threat that open-set tests cannot see (AUROC 0.500, chance level). The lightweight Transformer GLFormer, reimplemented from its paper (no code is public) and retrained on the same data, reaches 0.652 in the same detector with its published in-phase input and 0.849 when given the same I/Q input as our encoder.
item.dc:creator: Fawaz Abdul Razak, Bora Turgut, Mason Clark, Yasin Yilmaz

item.title: Carbon-Aware Joint Resource and Energy Scheduling for Cellular Base Stations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decarbonizing cellular networks requires coordinating communication-resource and battery operation with time-varying electricity prices and carbon intensity. We jointly optimize base station and battery operation under a carbon-adjusted electricity price and traffic-demand constraints, and solve the mixed-integer nonconvex problem through a two-stage decomposition exact under a minimum-power rule. Using California price and carbon-intensity data, we show that carbon-aware scheduling reduces emissions most when low-price and low-carbon periods are misaligned. Above a carbon price of roughly 100-300 USD/ton, battery operation shifts from cost-driven to carbon-driven, cutting emissions by up to 57.8% relative to a cost-only schedule.
item.dc:creator: Jaebum Park, Yutao Xie, Amitava Ghosh, Yuanyuan Shi, Robert W. Heath Jr

item.title: FFDT: Sim-to-Real Domain Transfer Method for Far-Field Ground Penetrating Radar
item.description: arXiv:2610.19265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scarcity of real-world ground penetrating radar (RealGPR) data is a major barrier to the development of deep learning (DL) methods for GPR data processing. Although simulated GPR (SimGPR) datasets can be used to train DL models, differences in hardware configuration and system parameters between SimGPR and RealGPR create a sim-to-real domain gap that leads to poor generalization of DL models to RealGPR measurements. To address this gap, we present a physics-based far-field GPR domain transfer (FFDT) method to transfer far-field SimGPR data to the corresponding RealGPR-domain data in the same scenario. In FFDT, SimGPR and RealGPR are modeled using angle-dependent transfer functions that capture three-dimensional antenna radiation characteristics. These transfer functions are then combined with ray tracing to enable the sim-to-real data transfer. Extensive studies across diverse objects and soil conditions demonstrate that FFDT-transferred data closely match RealGPR ground truth. To further demonstrate its value for RealGPR-domain dataset generation, FFDT is implemented to build a RealGPR-domain dataset for training a DL model for clutter removal. The model achieves robust performance on RealGPR measurements. With one-time SimGPR and RealGPR system calibration, FFDT enables RealGPR-domain dataset generation without requiring task-specific RealGPR field measurements for DL model training or fine-tuning, thereby addressing the RealGPR data scarcity bottleneck and supporting reliable development and deployment of DL methods for real-world GPR applications.
item.dc:creator: Chi Wang, Hai-Han Sun

item.title: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Integrated Sensing and Communication in IoT C-RAN
item.description: arXiv:2610.19612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with cloud radio access networks (C-RAN) unifies two foundational technologies for the Internet of Things (IoT), enabling both high-data-rate transmission and accurate environmental awareness. This paper investigates an uplink C-RAN system where multiple remote radio units (RRUs) jointly serve user equipment devices (UEs) and sense a target. We demonstrate that only a subset of RRUs is typically needed to meet sensing requirements, while energy is potentially conserved by deactivating redundant sensing RRUs. Motivated by this, we aim to improve the system's energy efficiency (EE) by jointly optimizing RRU activation, user association, and power allocation, while ensuring localization accuracy through the Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRLB). To address this problem, we propose a model-based iterative algorithm that integrates optimal user association, decision tree-based selection of sensing RRUs, and fixed-point power allocation. This algorithm is further used to train a graph neural network (GNN) framework, ISAC-GNN, to overcome scalability and computational complexity limitations. Our theoretical analysis ensures performance guarantees, while a semi-supervised training strategy enhances stability and generalization. Simulation results demonstrate that ISAC-GNN reduces inference time by 67% relative to the model-based approach, enabling real-time implementation for ISAC system resource management. In addition, ISAC-GNN allows scalable deployment across various system scenarios without retraining the model.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Internet of Things Journal, vol. 13, no. 9, pp. 18909-18929, 1 May1, 2026
item.dc:creator: Le Tung Giang, Nguyen Xuan Tung, Trinh Van Chien, Chau Yuen, Won-Joo Hwang

item.title: Hardware-friendly Baseband Design and Performance Analysis for LEO Broadband LoS-MIMO Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-frequency and broadband line-of-sight multiple-input multiple-output (LoS-MIMO) is a key solution for massive space-to-Earth data downlinks. However, in low Earth orbit (LEO) scenarios, it faces spatial rank deficiency from time-frequency coupling correlation and clock deviations from distributed oscillators. This paper establishes a dynamic effective channel throughput (ECT) framework incorporating waterfall characteristics of forward error correction. A hardware-friendly OFDM-based transceiver architecture with subband-adaptive truncation and dynamic timing recovery to achieve robust spatial decoupling is proposed. Through rigorous closed-form derivations, the equivalent signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) under joint errors is quantified, and an optimal scheduling algorithm combining truncation with variable coding and modulation is proposed to maximize ECT. Simulations confirm that the design circumvents outages caused by spatial notches with low complexity, stably enhancing the potential average throughput of a single dual-polarized beam to over 100 Gbps, providing a reliable theoretical foundation and baseband solution for next-generation high-throughput satellites.
item.dc:creator: Peixin Zhang, Fengkui Gong, Guo Li, Tony Q. S. Quek

item.title: Simultaneous Secure Communications and Sensing Privacy with Full Duplex MIMO Radios
item.description: arXiv:2610.19826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a Full Duplex (FD) framework for safeguarding Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) against a passive multi-antenna Eavesdropper (Eve). The adversary is modeled as both a communication and sensing threat, seeking to decode uplink data streams and estimate the surrounding scene. Eve's threat is quantified through two worst-case requirements over a location uncertainty region: a minimum secrecy rate for data confidentiality and a minimum eavesdropping Cramer-Rao Bound (CRB) for sensing privacy. We derive the eavesdropping information measures governing both data interception and scene inference, showcasing that transmitting Artificial Noise (AN) can degrade Eve's capabilities through the inverse interference-plus-noise covariance. Exploiting the underlying structure of the problem, we characterize finite-power local and robust feasibility conditions for target secrecy-privacy pairs. The analysis showcases that AN is fundamentally subspace-limited: increasing power is beneficial only along Eve's communication channel and sensing-derivative directions illuminated by the effective AN subspace. Finally, we formulate an AN power allocation problem that is solved via monotone branch-and-bound, and numerical evaluations quantify the AN power required to guarantee joint secrecy and sensing privacy.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Gavras, George C. Alexandropoulos

item.title: Comparative Analysis and Behavioral Modelling of Power Amplifiers in FR3
item.description: arXiv:2610.19889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power amplifier (PA) nonlinearity is a critical transmitter impairment in the upper mid-band (7 GHz to 24 GHz), designated as Frequency Range 3 (FR3) in emerging 6G standardisation. The 3GPP PA model baseline, TR 38.803 Annex A, was derived from 2.1 GHz and 28 GHz measurements and has not been revisited yet for FR3 standards work. This paper addresses that gap with characterisation measurements of multiple PA devices-under-test (DUTs), driven into gain compression in the 7 GHz and 15 GHz bands with 100 MHz and 200 MHz bandwidth. Memoryless polynomial and Generalized Memory Polynomial (GMP) behavioral models are extracted by least-squares regression and compared with 3GPP models spanning FR1 and FR2. The GaN PA DUT is modelled best at a higher nonlinear order and shows markedly stronger phase distortion than the wideband PA. The memory terms of the GMP model measurably improve the Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) at all operating points. An orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ambiguity function analysis from the Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) literature, using the extracted models, illustrates how PA compression raises the sidelobe floor of the sensing response. These results provide a reference for PA impairment modelling in FR3, directly applicable to ISAC system design. All model coefficients and measurement data are publicly available [1].
item.dc:creator: Cel Thys, Rodney Martinez Alonso, Ali H Alsarraf, Zhuangzhuang Cui, Dominique Schreurs, Sofie Pollin

item.title: DeepPV-MRF: End-to-End Partial-Volume Fraction Estimation from MR Fingerprinting Time Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.19894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background: Estimating subvoxel tissue fractions from magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is challenging. Conventional dictionary matching and segmentation pipelines can propagate errors from intermediate parametric maps into tissue fraction estimates. Purpose: We introduce DeepPV-MRF, a deep learning framework that directly estimates voxel-wise tissue fractions from raw MRF signals. Methods: A cascaded spatial-temporal network was trained on subject-derived Bloch simulations with radial k-space undersampling. The network combines temporal encoding and spatial U-Net refinement to estimate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), gray matter (GM), and white matter (WM) fractions without intermediate T1/T2 maps. We compared DeepPV-MRF with partial-volume dictionary matching (PV-DM) and pseudoinverse estimation (PV-Pinv) using simulated and in vivo data. Results: DeepPV-MRF outperformed both methods across acquisition settings. In single-shot simulations, CSF/WM/GM mean absolute errors were 0.0418/0.0744/0.0757, versus 0.1281/0.2443/0.2958 for PV-DM and 0.2021/0.2793/0.2630 for PV-Pinv. Corresponding structural similarity values were 0.960/0.916/0.922. In vivo results showed sharper anatomical boundaries and smoother tissue transitions, while cross-shot analysis indicated improved consistency across volunteers. Conclusions: DeepPV-MRF enables accurate and efficient direct tissue fraction estimation from MRF signals, particularly with limited shots. Further validation is needed before clinical deployment.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Ding, Yang Gao, Zhuang Xiong, Feng Liu, Martijn A. Cloos, Jin Jin, Hongfu Sun

item.title: Toward Motion Capture Textiles: A Batteryless IMU Array Powered and Networked Through a Conductive-Fabric Bus
item.description: arXiv:2610.19969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motion capture is increasingly important in healthcare, rehabilitation, and sports applications. However, conventional vision-based systems require camera infrastructure and line-of-sight conditions, limiting their use in daily environments. This paper proposes a location-independent platform for motion capture, based on an array of IMU (inertial measurement unit) sensor nodes without individual wiring or onboard batteries, enabled by two-dimensional communication and power delivery over conductive fabric. Pipeline processing in each sensor node, combined with a token-passing protocol, enables collision-free and stable data acquisition at 50 Hz. Real-time three-dimensional reconstruction of flexible objects is further demonstrated by applying Hermite spline interpolation to orientation data from grid-aligned IMUs. Against a cylinder of known radius, the reconstructed surface deviates by 2.60 mm RMS over the 225 mm span of the array. The reconstruction is formulated for the quasi-static regime, and this letter empirically validates it in that regime. The hardware platform and communication protocol implemented in this work enable further investigation toward dynamic motion capture textiles.
item.dc:creator: Ryusei Miyakawa, Akihito Noda

item.title: Hybrid Monostatic and Bistatic Sensing for Target Localization in OFDM Systems under Phase Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.19987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In hybrid monostatic-bistatic orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) sensing, each sensing node receives a superposition of monostatic and bistatic target returns, whose phase-noise (PN) characteristics differ fundamentally due to oscillator sharing. While monostatic sensing benefits from partial PN cancellation through the common transmit-receive oscillator, bistatic sensing involves independent oscillators and is therefore more strongly affected by PN. In this paper, we characterize the joint residual differential PN statistics of these superimposed components in a centralized two-node sensing system and quantify their impact on target localization via theoretical lower bounds considering three different receivers: (i) PN-free ideal receiver, (ii) PN-aware receiver that exploits the joint PN statistics, and (iii) PN-ignorant receiver that neglects PN.
item.dc:creator: Luc\'ia Pallar\'es Rodr\'iguez, Musa Furkan Keskin, Alireza Pourafzal, Jos\'e A. L\'opez-Salcedo, Gonzalo Seco-Granados, Henk Wymeersch

item.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.20018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. Transistor-level SKY130 simulations show that the second run gives the gradient within 1.9%; that hardware linearisation permits large, noise-robust error signals; that a 13-cell network learns the Iris data set; and that learning in situ restores mismatched circuits on which software-trained weights fail, from 53-63% to 88-96% test accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Craig Jin, Thomas Chaffey

item.title: Sampling Reduction for Near-Field to Far-Field Transformation of Bistatic Radar Target Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.20076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate bistatic radar cross-section (RCS) characterization requires near-field measurements over multiple dimensions, which, under typical near-field sampling requirements, can lead to long measurement durations for electrically large radar targets. This paper presents a near-field-to-far-field transformation based on an equivalent surface-current reconstruction using a-priori information about the target to reduce the number of newly acquired near-field samples. It is assumed that the prior target and the target under test (TUT) differ by localized geometrical modifications. Their complex differential near field is reconstructed using Tikhonov-regularized least squares QR factorization (LSQR) method. The reconstructed differential far- field contribution is coherently combined with the prior far-field contribution to estimate the bi-static RCS of the TUT. The method is preliminarily evaluated using simulations of a complex target at 6 GHz. The results indicate that, for the investigated simulation case, prior information can be used to thin out the sampling grid by 90% while maintaining close agreement with the simulation baseline.
item.dc:creator: Getahun Kibret Tadesse, Thomas Dallmann

item.title: Radial-Angular Resolution Framework for Near-Field Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.20092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-field beamfocusing confines radiated power into a localized three-dimensional focal spot, making the analytical characterization of radial and angular resolution critical for sixth-generation (6G) multi-user systems, yet existing models treat the focal resolution as a fixed geometric outcome rather than a tunable design variable. Based on the Angular Representation (ASR) approach, this paper presents a resolution framework to design contiguous focal regions across both the radial and angular domain for steered multi-user systems. By extending the definition of a tunable inter-beam overlap $\rho$, we derive closed-form expressions for the radial and angular focal boundaries and extents, alongside the steering-dependent minimum focal distance $d_{0,\text{min}}$ and maximum steering angle $\theta_{\text{max}}$. Using these boundaries, iterative synthesis algorithms are developed to construct uniform and non-uniform radial and angular beam arrangements. Finally, by analyzing both isolated and joint radial-angular configurations, we quantify the fundamental trade-offs between $\rho$, achievable user capacity, inter-user interference, and system sum-rate across varying steering angles.
item.dc:creator: Viviana Centritto, Sotiris Droulias, Angeliki Alexiou

item.title: Movable-Antenna Relay Enhanced Multiuser Communications: Reinforcement Learning-Based Antenna Positioning and Power Allocation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Movable antenna (MA) has emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communication performance by flexibly reconfiguring wireless channels via antenna movement. In this paper, we propose an MA relay-enhanced multiuser communication system that adopts a half-duplex decode-and-forward (DF) relay scheme. The relay node is equipped with an MA array, and a buffer is employed to enhance the end-to-end transmission performance. Specifically, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the minimum average achievable rate among multiple users over a given transmission period by dynamically optimizing the positions of MAs, transmit power, and beamforming matrices, subject to the constraints on antenna movement, inter-antenna spacing, and total energy budget for antenna movement and transmission. To address this non-convex problem with highly coupled variables, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based algorithm, where a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm is utilized to optimize the antenna positions and power allocation, while the transmit and receive beamforming solutions are obtained through closed-form expressions in each time slot. Numerical results validate the efficacy of the proposed RL-based algorithm and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed MA relay-enhanced multiuser communication system over the conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA)-based relay system and other MA-based benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Yuanjun Zhang, Lipeng Zhu, Haobin Mao, Zhe Li, Zhenyu Xiao

item.title: Radar-Only Long-Term Beam Prediction in mmWave Vehicular Networks: An Empirical Study of Doppler Input and Cross-Modal Distillation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensing-aided beam prediction could cut the beam-training overhead of millimeter-wave vehicular links, and two design choices could strengthen a radar-only predictor: a Doppler-resolved input and knowledge distilled from a camera during training. We measure what each is worth in received power rather than in top-1 accuracy, whose differences of a few points amount to only tenths of a decibel. We use real DeepSense 6G measurements, mainly at one roadside site, and one convolutional-recurrent predictor family evaluated open-loop up to 0.67 s ahead. Adding a range-Doppler map to the range-angle map lowers the mean beam-selection loss by 0.28 dB (95% bootstrap interval [0.14, 0.41]). The gain comes from the Doppler content, not from the extra input, and replicates, as pre-specified, at a second base station, although holding the last measured beam beats both predictors there. Cross-modal knowledge distillation from a motion-mask vision-radar teacher, by contrast, changes received power by -0.01 dB ([-0.07, +0.06]). The tested teacher, student, fusion and distillation variants show the same null in the metric each was scored on. Where distillation helps, in an exploratory run with few training passes, a radar-only teacher trained on all training passes reproduces most of the gain. For this predictor family and the full training set, the measurable gain at the link comes from Doppler-resolved radar content; no tested route for transferring training-only visual information adds a resolved gain.
item.dc:creator: Jeongwan Kang, Miguel Bordallo L\'{o}pez, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Junhyeong Kim, Sunwoo Kim

item.title: Sensing-Aided Vehicular Beam Tracking: System Gain Over Link Feedback and Probe-Verified Sensing Invocation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensor-based beam prediction is usually evaluated against exhaustive beam training, leaving open when sensing adds useful information beyond a deployed tracker's link feedback and when it should be withheld. We separate system gain from the marginal value of sensing in action-restricted causal replay of recorded 64-beam sweeps from four vehicular DeepSense 6G scenarios. The replay exposes only serving-beam and explicitly probed candidate powers and counts probes and model invocations separately. The proposed controller combines a scheduled post-setup re-sweep with probe-verified sensing admission and blacklist backoff. In three scenarios where feedback-only tracking is within 0.25 dB of the recorded-sweep oracle, the controller stays close to feedback-only in mean loss while rarely invoking the model, whereas always-on sensing performs worse. In the sole high-innovation scenario, the controller's system gain is 0.82 dB (95% confidence interval [0.30, 1.40]) over the plain feedback-only tracker and 0.15 dB over a probe-limited re-sweeping reference, with fewer probes than either. Sensing and the re-sweep both correct setup lock loss. At the native decision interval, enabling sensing in the same controller yields no statistically resolved loss reduction but cuts probing by 21%. In this scenario, accurate sensing reduces loss relative to the sensor-disabled controller under emulated link noise, staleness or longer decision intervals. Weak or delayed sensing can instead increase loss despite probe verification. These exploratory results characterize sensing as a conditional substitute for RF probing or a source of loss reduction, depending on the limitations of link feedback and on the accuracy and timeliness of sensing.
item.dc:creator: Jeongwan Kang, Miguel Bordallo L\'{o}pez, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Junhyeong Kim, Sunwoo Kim

item.title: TRP-UE Bistatic Sensing for 6G Performance Analysis and Insights
item.description: arXiv:2610.20219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) equips cellular networks with the dual capability of data transmission and environmental sensing by sharing spectrum, waveforms, and radio hardware. While network-side sensing via transmission-reception points (TRPs) has been widely investigated, the use of user equipment (UEs) as sensing receivers introduces additional bistatic viewpoints and can improve target observability. UE-assisted operation is nevertheless constrained by small UE apertures and by waveform processing, especially when data-bearing communication signals are reused for sensing. The present paper investigates theoretical limits and operating conditions for UE-assisted passive target positioning, with emphasis on hybrid operation that fuses TRP--TRP and TRP--UE measurements. A unified OFDM-based signal-and-noise model is developed to cover both positioning reference signals (PRS) and communication waveform reuse with modulation-dependent noise enhancement. Based on this model, closed-form Fisher-information expressions and Cramer-Rao lower bounds are derived for delay and angular parameters and are mapped to positioning error bounds (PEBs) for two estimator classes: time-angle positioning based on TDOA + DoA and delay-only 3D ellipsoid positioning based on excess-delay/TDOA measurements. Monte-Carlo simulations across reference SNR, subcarrier spacing and occupied bandwidth, modulation order, radar cross section (RCS), sensing mode, and positioning algorithm identify regimes where UE participation and hybrid sensing provide significant gains and quantify the associated estimator-to-bound trade-offs.
item.dc:creator: Necati Kagan Erkek, Marco Di Renzo, Arman Shojaeifard, Yasser Mestrah, Remun Koirala, Mohammad Heggo, Kunjan Shah

item.title: FlowSep-RF: Rectified Flow Matching for Single-Channel Radio-Frequency Signal Separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-channel radio-frequency (RF) signal separation is important for interference mitigation when a signal of interest overlaps with a co-channel interferer in time and frequency. Classical matched filtering and LMMSE receivers are limited under structured non-Gaussian interference, while diffusion and score-based methods often require iterative sampling or optimization. We propose FlowSep-RF, a rectified flow matching framework that learns a clean-endpoint transport from the received mixture to the signal of interest. The model combines time-domain IQ samples with frequency-domain features and recovers the separated waveform using one endpoint velocity evaluation. We evaluate FlowSep-RF on QPSK mixtures with OFDM-BPSK, OFDM-QPSK, and RFChallenge CommSignal2 interference against classical, discriminative, and generative baselines. FlowSep-RF achieves the lowest average BER and MSE among evaluated baselines across all three settings with one-step inference.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Kamel, Tamer Nadeem

item.title: Beam-STeP: Generative Site-Specific Beam Prediction with Spatio-Temporal Priors
item.description: arXiv:2610.20282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A generative site-specific beam prediction (Beam-STeP) method is proposed. Spatial priors from site-specific propagation and mobility information are jointly exploited with temporal priors from historical beam observations for beam prediction. To address the beam prediction ambiguity from multimodal spatio-temporal priors, the generative model is adopted, where a history-conditioned diffusion model is proposed to learn the multimodal conditional distribution of future beamforming vectors. Multiple beam candidates are sampled from the distribution using a denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM). The candidate with the highest received power is then selected for transmission. Simulation results across three urban scenarios demonstrate that: i) Beam-STeP generally achieves higher normalized beamforming gains than the baselines under the same probing budget, particularly as beam prediction progresses; ii) site-specific propagation and mobility priors improve recursive beam prediction performance; and iii) DDIM sampling enables a flexible gain-latency trade-off.
item.dc:creator: Ziyue Wang, Zongyao Zhao, Zhaolin Wang, Yuanwei Liu

item.title: Opportunities for Direct-to-Cell Polarization MIMO in the S-band Downlink of a LEO Satellite Footprint
item.description: arXiv:2610.20296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A single low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite offers almost no spatial degrees of freedom. Its two polarizations, however, can be exploited to carry a second layer to a handset, which 5G New Radio (NR) non-terrestrial networks do not use yet. The gain of this layer in downlink spectral efficiency (SE) is mapped over the footprint of a satellite at 330 km altitude above Munich transmitting at 2 GHz. The channel is modeled as a cascade of Jones factors for the phased-array payload, Faraday rotation, a dual-polarized land mobile satellite (LMS) channel with a line of sight, and a standardized handset antenna element at three attitudes. For a handset with boresight pointing to zenith, ideal precoding selects rank 2 with a probability of at least 0.95 within about 340 km of the nadir point at a reference signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 6 dB. With closed-loop precoding, such a handset on the nadir track is in rank 2 during 99% of a pass. At 13 dB, rank selection with closed-loop precoding raises the mean SE over the footprint by 49%, and upright handsets gain about 31%. Their gain is limited to the positions where they face the satellite, since the element gain is low behind the handset. At 3 dB, these gains fall to 15% and 7%.
item.dc:creator: Rainer Bachl, Matteo Ferro, Bingguang Peng, Muhammad Nabeel

item.title: Dual-Polarized Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for mmWave Communications: A Practical Design and Prototype Implementation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a dual-polarized rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) design for millimeter-wave (mmWave) or frequency range 2 (FR2) communications. Focusing on a practical implementation, we consider the specific scenario of a single transmitter serving two receivers (users) within the same time, frequency, and code resource block. The transmitter and each receiver are equipped with a pair of dual-polarized antennas. We first present the system formulation and compute the achievable rate expressions for discrete constellations. Based on these expressions, we propose and evaluate two receiver architectures: one based on successive interference cancellation (SIC) and a non-SIC decoder. Both designs exhibit comparable performance, and the combination of polarization diversity and RSMA provides the system with significant flexibility to adapt to different channel conditions when serving both users, while the non-SIC decoder enables a simpler hardware implementation. We then present a prototype implementation of the proposed design, operating at a carrier frequency of 25 GHz, and evaluate it by measuring the symbol error rate (SER) of the different data streams under various signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and polarization diversity conditions. The obtained measurements show good agreement with software simulations, thereby validating the system implementation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first mmWave RSMA prototype reported in the literature and the first to exploit polarization diversity. Furthermore, given the selected carrier frequency, the proposed design may also find applicability in the upper portion of the envisioned FR3 band (7-24 GHz).
item.dc:creator: \'Alvaro Pend\'as-Recondo, \'Alvaro F. Vaquero, Jes\'us Alberto L\'opez-Fern\'andez, Marcos R. Pino

item.title: To Stack or Not to Stack? Jacobian Conditioning and the Benefits of Depth in Metasurface-Based Linear Transformation Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.20377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates when and why stacking programmable metasurfaces into Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) improves linear transformation synthesis at a fixed phase-control budget. The analysis shows that algebraic Jacobian rank alone is insufficient to characterize practical synthesis, which also depends on the strength and balance of the sensitivity directions generated by the available controls. A layer-resolved analysis of the cascade model explains how inter-layer propagation can generate complementary sensitivity directions. The relevance of this mechanism is then assessed using an S-parameter multiport model that includes electromagnetic coupling and multiple scattering. Numerical results in near- and far-field sensing scenarios show that distributing the same control resources across multiple layers can strengthen weak transformation directions, improve Jacobian conditioning, and substantially enhance synthesis accuracy. These findings explain why increasing depth can offer benefits that are not obtained by simply enlarging a single programmable surface, and identify layer complementarity and Jacobian conditioning as useful criteria for SIM architecture design.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Abrardo, Andrea Garulli

item.title: Modeling Diffuse Scattering in Mobility Scenarios: Ray Tracing Model and Measurement Validation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-source ray tracing (RT) frameworks are increasingly used for site-specific channel modeling due to their reproducibility and extensibility. In non-stationary mobility scenarios, repeated RT evaluations can generate different diffuse propagation paths without preserving their correspondence, limiting a consistent representation of their temporal evolution. To address this limitation, we extend diffuse scattering modeling in Sionna RT using persistent surface-associated scattering points. Their positions remain fixed, while their contributions evolve according to changes in the propagation geometry and visibility. The proposed approach is validated using empirical radio channel impulse response measurements in an urban vehicular scenario at 5.9 GHz. Compared with the standard Sionna RT baseline, the proposed model shows improved agreement with measurements in the delay and Doppler domains.
item.dc:creator: Milica Djordjevic, Thomas Wilding, Anja Daki\'c, Markus Hofer, Benjamin Rainer, Thomas Zemen

item.title: Train to Stitch: Topology-Preserving Regularization for Interoperable Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19401v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large, powerful pre-trained models become more prevalent, there is growing interest in developing methods that allow different neural networks to be seamlessly combined with little or no direct communication between them. Take autoencoder-based data compression as an example: the ability to independently choose architectures and train encoder and decoder models, while still ensuring they work together, could fundamentally transform how such models are built, deployed, and updated. In this work, we introduce a novel approach that leverages topological regularization to align the latent spaces of two independently trained autoencoder models, entirely eliminating the need for coordination during training. We provide a conditional theoretical analysis showing how the structural agreement encouraged by our regularizer can translate into approximate geometric compatibility between independently learned representations. Reconstruction experiments validate this approach empirically, substantially narrowing the interoperability gap across multiple datasets.
item.dc:creator: Akshay Malhotra, Nicolas Zilberstein, Shahab Hamidi-Rad

item.title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition
item.description: arXiv:2610.19722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classification, and MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Cao, Jichao Zhang, Xiao-Lei Zhang

item.title: Resilient Angle-Constrained Formation Control and Localization Under DoS Attacks (Extended Version)
item.description: arXiv:2610.19824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies resilient angle-constrained leader--follower formation control and localization of multi-agent systems under asynchronous denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, which block individual sensing and communication links. To preserve the well-posedness of angle-based localization, an all-or-nothing triangle integrity protocol (ANTIP) is proposed to convert edge-wise attacks into triangle-wise ones, and DoS attacks are classified into localizability-maintained and localizability-broken attacks. First, with relative position measurements over attack-free links, resilient formation tracking laws are designed for leaders with constant velocities and with time-varying velocities comprising translational, rotational, and scaling motions. These laws guarantee asymptotic tracking and finite-time recovery of tracking, respectively, when the duration of localizability-broken attacks is suitably bounded. Second, with only angle measurements and communications, a resilient simultaneous localization and formation control (RSLAF) scheme is developed. It combines a finite-time distributed observer, which estimates the exosystem matrices and states under asynchronous DoS attacks, with a perturbation-based localization law that prevents localization from getting stuck at degenerate configurations. The theoretical results are rigorously proved and illustrated by numerical simulations.
item.dc:creator: Nhat-Minh Le-Phan, Ziliang Lyu, Lihua Xie

item.title: Bilinear Compressive Security with Finitely Many Samples
item.description: arXiv:2610.19898v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bilinear Compressive Security (BCS) is a lightweight encryption scheme that combines compressed sensing with a fresh random convolution filter to improve resistance against key-recovery attacks under key reuse. Previous work derived information-theoretic guarantees for BCS by relating key identifiability to phase retrieval under the assumption that an adversary has access to the full ciphertext distribution induced by the random filter. In practice, however, an adversary only observes finitely many encryptions, leaving the security of BCS in the finite-sample regime largely unexplored. In this paper, we study key recovery from only finitely many observations. We first develop a covariance-based attack that estimates the linear measurements from repeated encryptions of the same plaintext and subsequently recovers the secret measurement matrix. We analyze the estimation procedure and derive finite-sample guarantees together with corresponding sample-complexity bounds. We further investigate the complete attack experimentally and compare its observed recovery behavior with the previously established information-theoretic identifiability results. Our experiments show two qualitatively different recovery regimes on the structure of the measurement matrix. For dense matrices, including Gaussian matrices, the number of measurements required for successful recovery appears to grow linearly with the signal dimension. This differs from the worst-case behavior suggested by information theory. In contrast, for matrices with sparse rows, we observe a quadratic growth consistent with the theoretical bound. These results suggest that the sparsity structure of the measurement matrix plays an important role in the security of BCS and should be taken into account when selecting parameters and designing practical instances of the scheme.
item.dc:creator: Axel Flinth, Semira Einsele, Matilda Kylberg, Hubert Orlicki, Gerhard Wunder

item.title: Exact Cap Response and Aperture Selection for Molecular Communication under Aligned Drift
item.description: arXiv:2610.20233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial reception under directed molecule transport requires balancing useful molecule capture against intersymbol interference (ISI). To characterize this balance, we study a fully absorbing spherical receiver that counts absorption events only within a prescribed cap. Using the known joint first-hitting law under aligned drift, we derive exact cap impulse, cumulative, and eventual responses. We perform stable cumulative evaluation. We then assess the derived responses through particle simulations and time-step comparisons, and demonstrate that our conditional-timing analysis explains when opposite drifts of equal magnitude can favor the same wider aperture. We also show that for the studied geometry and a symbol duration of $0.15$ s, the aperture that maximizes the signal-to-interference difference (SID) increases from $29.13^\circ$ at zero drift to $61.86^\circ$ at a drift magnitude of $40$ $\mu$m/s. These results (i) connect joint arrival-time and location statistics to spatial reception design, (ii) characterize the tradeoff between useful molecule capture and ISI, (iii) support SID-based aperture selection for a given drift and symbol duration, and (iv) quantify the SID loss incurred by retaining the zero-drift optimal aperture for the same symbol duration.
item.dc:creator: Yen-Chi Lee, Chun-An Yang, Nan Yang

item.title: The Derivation of The Probability of Error for BPSK, 16-QAM and 64-QAM in Rayleigh Fading Channel: A Unified Approach
item.description: arXiv:2406.16548v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding the probability of error is paramount in the design and analysis of digital communication systems, particularly in Rayleigh fading channels where signal impairments are prevalent. This article presents a unified approach for deriving the probability of error formulations applicable to Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK), 16-Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (16-QAM), and 64-QAM in Rayleigh fading channels. This article presents a general approach to derive the probability of error formulations applicable to Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK), 16-Quadruple Amplitude Modulation (16-QAM) and 64-QAM in Rayleigh fading channels. The derivation process encompasses the unique characteristics of each modulation scheme and the statistical properties of Rayleigh fading providing a comprehensive framework to analyze error performance. By establishing a unified formulation, this approach simplifies the analysis and facilitates a deeper understanding of error probability behavior across different modulation schemes. The derived formulations offer insights into the impact of fading-induced impairments on system performance, allowing for accurate prediction and optimization of communication systems in real-world fading environments. The insights and techniques presented herein serve as a valuable resource for researchers, engineers, and practitioners engaged in the design and optimization of communication systems operating in challenging fading environments.
item.dc:creator: Amr Abdelbari

item.title: What If They Took the Shot? A Hierarchical Bayesian Framework for Counterfactual Expected Goals
item.description: arXiv:2511.23072v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How would the probability of scoring change if a different player took the same shot? Although expected goals models describe the difficulty of scoring opportunities, comparing players on identical chances requires accounting for uncertainty in their estimated conversion probabilities. We address this question through a hierarchical Bayesian framework that evaluates alternative shooters under the same observed circumstances. Using 35,700 eligible shots from four leagues during the 2015/16 season, we compare a contextual benchmark with a primary player-intercept model and a provisional extension that allows player differences to vary with shooting conditions. Paired posterior draws preserve shared uncertainty when individual probability differences are aggregated across opportunities. Chronological validation demonstrates improved predictive performance relative to a constant-rate baseline, but introducing player effects provides negligible additional gains. Controlled single-seed experiments show that greater information per player improves estimation accuracy and narrows uncertainty intervals, although distinguishing small differences remains difficult and confident conclusions about near-null effects can become more frequent. Applications involving Giroud--Vardy and Berardi--Sansone similarly yield estimated differences that are small relative to their posterior uncertainty. These findings highlight an important distinction between predicting the outcome of a shot and establishing whether one player would be more likely to convert it. The proposed framework makes this distinction explicit by evaluating alternative shooters on fixed recorded opportunities while accounting for their contextual exposure. The resulting comparisons concern conditional conversion rather than the causal consequences of replacing a player in a match.
item.dc:creator: Mikayil Mahmudlu, Oktay Karaku\c{s}, Hasan Arkada\c{s}, Can Ey\"{u}po\u{g}lu

item.title: UPSim: UxNB Propagation Simulator for 3D Map-Driven FR3 Deployments
item.description: arXiv:2605.17378v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce UPSim (UxNB Propagation Simulator), an open-source, Ray Tracing-calibrated solution for spatially consistent FR3 (16.95 GHz) air-to-ground propagation modeling in Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. Instead of executing point-to-point ray launches for every ground position, UPSim derives deterministic visibility regions directly from global 3D building geometry (3D-GloBFP) via fast shadow projection. It then augments these regions with Line-of-Sight (LOS) state-specific, UAV height- and distance-dependent path loss, spatially correlated large-scale fading, and log-logistic small-scale fading parameterized by over 136 million Ray Tracing (RT) channels. Validation against reference RT data demonstrates that UPSim accurately reproduces empirical attenuation maps, outperforming the 3GPP baseline by reducing the aggregate Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance from 0.33 to 0.04. The resulting maps enable route-based analysis of channel evolution in complex urban layouts, capturing critical trajectory-level metrics such as spatial outage persistence. Consequently, UPSim provides a highly scalable, open-source middle ground between computationally expensive full RT and purely stochastic models for mobility-aware 6G aerial network planning.
item.dc:creator: Evgenii Vinogradov

item.title: Stochastic Analysis of Successive Interference Cancellation in a Narrow-Beam LEO Uplink
item.description: arXiv:2607.11620v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates uplink coverage probability, i.e., the SIR distribution, and SIR order statistics at a low Earth orbit satellite base station (LEO BS) with narrow Gaussian antenna beams. The user equipments (UEs) connected to the satellite radio access network are distributed according to a Poisson point process (PPP) on the Earth's surface. We propose a novel framework for stochastic geometry analysis of the SIR using a Gaussian mixture shadowing model, derive tractable expressions for the mean, variance, and probability density function, and analyze the SIR distributions for the three strongest UEs under successive interference cancellation (SIC). Furthermore, we propose a gamma distribution model for the interference distribution. We show that SIC enables each LEO BS to serve multiple UEs per beam cell, improving user fairness while preserving the network throughput. The observations imply design recommendations for next-generation non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) LEO networks. The analytical insights are validated against Monte Carlo simulations.
item.dc:creator: Ilari Angervuori, Risto Wichman

item.title: Low-Complexity Channel Estimation Framework for Non-Square UPA-Assisted XL-MIMO Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.18744v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-complexity channel state information acquisition is crucial for extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems. However, practical deployments of non-square uniform planar arrays (UPAs) in hybrid-field environments face prohibitive computational complexity and degraded estimation accuracy due to limited elevation angle-of-arrival (AoA) resolution and deteriorated channel sparsity. To tackle these challenges, we propose a low-complexity channel estimation framework. First, an antenna-domain extrapolation scheme synthesizes a virtually enlarged vertical aperture via the spatial correlation among adjacent elements, breaking the elevation resolution limit. The framework then disentangles the parameter coupling by transforming the two-dimensional joint search into two sequential one-dimensional searches. Specifically, elevation AoAs are extracted via an extrapolation-enhanced discrete Fourier transform-Newtonized orthogonal matching pursuit (NOMP) algorithm along the virtually enlarged vertical uniform linear array (ULA), while azimuth AoAs, ranges, and gains are acquired utilizing a discrete fractional Fourier transform-NOMP algorithm along a horizontal ULA. A subspace fitting-driven path matching algorithm pairs these decoupled parameters. To overcome the accuracy bottleneck of the antenna-domain scheme, a correlation-domain extrapolation scheme is further developed by exploiting the structural properties of the spatial correlation matrix to decouple the near-field quadratic and azimuth phase components, yielding a noise-suppressed virtual array. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
item.dc:creator: Yilong Liu, Xi Yang, Binggui Zhou, Yu Han, Ting Liu, Shaodan Ma

item.title: A Knowledge-Centric Communication For Autonomous Cislunar Networks
item.description: arXiv:2608.04817v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Future lunar infrastructure requires communication as a persistent service rather than a mission specific capability. Communication, digital twin, and artificial intelligence (AI) research have advanced autonomy independently while largely assuming that system state can eventually be reconciled with ground truth. Cislunar communication violates this assumption because propagation delay is fundamentally limited by the speed of light, visibility is governed by orbital geometry, and autonomous decisions often precede confirming observations. Here we introduce a knowledge-centric communication framework in which a digital twin continuously integrates delayed observations, communication physics, learned models, uncertainty quantification, and mission objectives into an evolving Operational Knowledge State. To quantify what is known, how uncertain it remains, and how current it is, we define two quantities over the fused Bayesian belief maintained for each communication link: \emph{Knowledge Entropy}, the differential entropy of the posterior belief, and \emph{Knowledge Freshness}, which generalizes Age of Information (AoI) from a single information stream to the temporal validity of the fused Operational Knowledge State. We prove that distributed knowledge fusion systematically improves operational knowledge by reducing uncertainty and demonstrate its importance for mission success through simulations and comparisons with flight data from the Longjiang-2 lunar micro-satellite.
item.dc:creator: Afan Ali, Daniel Benevides da Costa, Ali Arshad Nasir

item.title: Antenna Positioning and Beamforming Optimization in MA Enabled Secure ISAC Systems: A Gradient-Based Meta Learning Approach
item.description: arXiv:2608.12870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) significantly improves spectral efficiency but introduces security risks regarding the interception of embedded communication signals. This paper proposes an movable antenna (MA)-enabled secure ISAC system that utilizes the spatial degrees of freedom of MA to mitigate these risks. Then, a problem is formulated to maximize the system secrecy rate by jointly optimizing antenna positioning, transmit beamforming, and artificial noise. However, the principal challenge arises from the non-convexity of the optimization problem and the strong coupling of the optimization variables. Generally, traditional optimization methods for this problem suffer from complex mathematical derivations, while existing deep learning approaches rely heavily on the training data distribution. To address these issues, we introduce a gradient-based meta learning (GML) algorithm, which works without pre-training and demonstrates favorable performance. Specifically, the algorithm establishes a neural network for each optimization variable, where the gradient of the objective function with respect to the variable serves as the input, and the output of the network determines the variable's update step. By handling the constraints and constructing penalty terms, the global loss function is used to guide the optimization process. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves satisfactory performance in terms of both communication security and sensing capabilities.
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Li, Yujie Zhao, Zhou Su, Xiao Tang, Zhiqing Wei, Ying Wang, Wen Chen

item.title: Low-complexity Soft-decision LLR Calculations for Next-generation IM-DD Systems with RIN
item.description: arXiv:2608.20102v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The demand for higher speeds in intra-data center interconnects will eventually require high-order pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) combined with soft-decision (SD) forward error correction (FEC). The laser relative intensity noise (RIN) is an important noise impairment that limits the performance of high-speed intensity-modulation (IM) and direct-detection (DD) systems, as it induces a channel with signal-dependent noise. In this paper, we show that an accurate calculation of the log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) is critical for the performance of the SD-FEC decoder in RIN-dominated IM-DD systems. First, we show that assuming signal-independent additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) statistics to compute LLRs results in a significant penalty in performance. As an alternative, we propose a low-complexity piecewise linear approximation of the exact LLRs of Gray-coded PAM-4 and PAM-8 for the RIN-dominated IM-DD channel. We show using the generalized mutual information that our approximation results in no performance loss versus using exact LLRs, unlike the AWGN-like assumption. Furthermore, we validate the analysis with bit error rate (BER) performance of SD decoding. We show that our approximation matches the BERs achieved using exact LLRs. Therefore, our approximation avoids a BER error floor penalty of up to 7.2 times using an extended Hamming code with PAM-4, and up to 2.41 dB of optical modulation amplitude penalty using high-code-rate low-density parity-check codes with PAM-8 for the same target BER.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Villenas, Yunus Can G\"ultekin, Alex Alvarado

item.title: ALF: Spectrally Anchored Latent Flow Matching for Wireless Signal Generation
item.description: arXiv:2609.36385v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wireless time-series generation is useful for emerging applications that will drive the adoption and integration of machine learning tasks within next-generation networks, such as waveform classification in shared spectrum bands and interpretation of the physical world through integrated sensing and communications. Unlike a generic time series, wireless signals have time-frequency duality, where a frequency domain bandwidth constraint implicitly imposes latent structural constraints on the evolution of the time-domain sequence. In this paper, we develop Anchored Latent Flow (ALF), a latent space flow model for label-conditioned signal generation that exploits this duality. Our flow model "reasons'" through a spectrogram, which is a 2-D representation of the signal constructed by applying a windowed Fast Fourier Transform to successive, overlapping signal segments and mapping their frequency-domain power components across time. Specifically, we shape the latent space of the flow model through a training-time auxiliary objective that is supervised by the (latent) spectrogram (i.e., anchoring through the spectrogram). By guiding the flow field to reason through a spectrogram, the generated sequence maintains long-range coherence across time and greatly improves the signal quality at inference. Empirically, ALF exhibits state-of-the-art generation quality and reconstruction error across various signal lengths, waveform classes, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and channel conditions, reaching a train on synthetic, test on real (TSTR) accuracy of 84.5%, a 1.9X average memory reduction, and 100X average compute speedup over existing models. Our design further enables downstream tasks, including style transfer and data augmentation, and has broad utility for the wireless community.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Li, Sai Shankar Narasimhan, Priam Alataris, Avi Bagchi, Kaushik Chowdhury, Sanjay Shakkottai

item.title: RRM-GPT: A Framework and Vision for Radio Resource Management Foundation Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.04296v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Learning-based models for radio resource management (RRM) are typically built for a single function and deployment, so each new setting repeats the development pipeline. RRM decisions, however, share a common structure: each is assembled from interdependent fields, defined by the standard, whose values are selected in view of the network state. We propose RRM-GPT, an autoregressive framework for RRM foundation models that generate these decisions as a language model generates text. An encoder maps heterogeneous network observations into a common token representation, and a decoder emits the decision one field at a time, each conditioned on the network state and the fields already committed. Pretraining on unannotated network logs teaches the model what makes a decision valid and how controllers choose among valid decisions; post-training then adapts it to deployment-specific operator objectives through imitation or reinforcement learning. The framework targets two forms of reuse: a function-specific model reused across deployments, and a model shared across RRM functions that generates their interdependent decisions as one sequence. In a 5G New Radio (NR) case study, we demonstrate that a single model generates complete scheduling grants spanning user selection, timing, link adaptation, resource allocation, and control signaling. The model captures dependencies among grant fields and transfers learned behavior to an unseen scenario without adaptation.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Aboulfotouh, Akram Bin Sediq, Koosha Pourtahmasi Roshandeh, Omar Mashaal, Ahmad M. Nagib, Jale Sadreddini, Hatem Abou-Zeid

item.title: A Wireless World Model for AI-Native 6G Networks
item.description: arXiv:2603.25216v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrating AI into the physical layer is a cornerstone of 6G networks. However, current data-driven approaches struggle to generalize across dynamic environments because they lack an intrinsic understanding of electromagnetic wave propagation. We introduce the Wireless World Model (WWM), a multi-modal foundation framework predicting the spatiotemporal evolution of wireless channels by internalizing the causal relationship between 3D geometry and signal dynamics. Pre-trained on a massive ray-traced multi-modal dataset, WWM overcomes the data authenticity gap, further validated under real-world measurement data. Using a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a multi-modal mixture-of-experts Transformer, WWM fuses channel state information, 3D point clouds, and user trajectories into a unified representation. Across the five key downstream tasks supported by WWM, it achieves remarkable performance in seen environments, unseen generalization scenarios, and real-world measurements, consistently outperforming SOTA uni-modal foundation models and task-specific models. This paves the way for physics-aware 6G intelligence that adapts to the physical world.
item.dc:creator: Ziqi Chen, Yi Ren, Yixuan Huang, Qi Sun, Nan Li, Yuhong Huang, Yifan Li, Liang Xia

item.title: CORTEG: Foundation Models Enable Cross-Modality Representation Transfer from Scalp to Intracranial Brain Recordings
item.description: arXiv:2605.10337v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Intracranial electrocorticography (ECoG) offers high signal-to-noise access to cortical activity for brain-computer interfaces, yet limited per-patient data has led most prior work to rely on small, subject-specific decoders that neglect information shared across patients. We investigate whether large pretrained scalp-EEG foundation models (EEG FMs) can be adapted to ECoG, enabling cross-patient learning and competitive decoding performance while calibrating to a held-out patient in 10-30 minutes on a single GPU. We introduce CORTEG, a cross-modality transfer framework that combines a pretrained EEG FM backbone, an electrode-aware KNNSoftFourier spatial adapter, a dual-stream tokenizer for low-frequency and high-gamma activity, and a leave-one-subject-out fine-tuning strategy. We evaluate CORTEG on two challenging regression tasks: public finger-trajectory regression ($n=9$) and private audio-envelope regression ($n=16$). CORTEG achieves state-of-the-art mean performance on both tasks, achieving the highest mean correlation among the compared methods on the public finger benchmark and larger, statistically significant gains on the audio task and in low-data-per-patient calibration. We further validate CORTEG on the public BrainTreebank stereo-EEG classification tasks, where it also performs strongly. Furthermore, CORTEG outperforms the compared intracranial-EEG foundation models across the continuous regression tasks. Feature analyses align with neurophysiology, and latent representations capture low-dimensional finger-movement structure. Together, these results provide systematic evidence that scalp-EEG pretraining can be repurposed across intracranial recording modalities and tasks, enabling data-efficient neural decoders that can adapt to new patients.
item.dc:creator: Liuyin Yang, Qiang Sun, Bob Van Dyck, Eva Calvo Merino, Marc M. Van Hulle

item.title: Structured Masked Diffusion for Shared-Codebook Unsourced Random Access Decoding
item.description: arXiv:2605.26580v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In shared-codebook unsourced random access (URA), a receiver must recover an unordered set of messages from simultaneous transmissions. Its outer decoder assembles ambiguous slot-wise evidence into distinct codewords while enforcing parity constraints. We propose CIDER, a learned outer decoder that combines masked-diffusion refinement with cross-row demixing and parity-aware propagation on the code's Tanner graph. At higher per-bin loads, quality-guided remasking selectively re-decodes low-confidence rows. On the evaluated GF(64) LDPC codes at $K=2$, CIDER has lower measured symbol and codeword error rates than SIC-BP and FFT-BP at all four code lengths. In same-GPU decoder-only measurements, the deployed mixed-precision implementation is $8.2\times$ to $167\times$ faster than our optimized FFT-BP implementation across those lengths. We also evaluate higher loads, estimated user counts, and detector mismatch. Code is available at https://github.com/jiyunyoung/CIDER/tree/neurips-2026.
item.dc:creator: Taekyun Lee, Jiyoung Yun, Jeffrey G. Andrews, Hyeji Kim

item.title: Gauge-Invariant, Parameter-Insensitive Regularization for Potential Recovery from Flow on Directed Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.13609v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recovering a latent potential from observed flow on a directed graph (a discrete Poisson problem with Dirichlet boundaries) is ill-posed, and the standard fix backfires: ridge regularization shrinks toward a gauge-meaningless origin, collapsing and reversing the recovered ordering ($+0.81\to-0.42$ rank correlation against a planted ground truth). The gauge-invariant graph Dirichlet energy removes the hazard and delivers parameter-insensitivity: the estimate is stable across four orders of magnitude in $\lambda$, whereas ridge inverts the ordering for every $\lambda>0$. We prove the reduced solve is SPD and preserves dynamic range exactly where ridge collapses it, and localize absorbing boundaries from flow alone via a Poisson residual. The $H^1$ seminorm is classical; what is new is the gauge diagnosis, the parameter-insensitivity it buys, and an ablation showing the result is robust to the extraction method. On three public clickstream corpora the gauge-invariant estimate retains $28$--$41\%$ of the interior dynamic range while ridge collapses to as little as $0.2\%$. The same gauge invariance carries into graph neural networks -- neutralizing the constant mode per layer prevents the oversmoothing that collapses a deep directed GCN -- linking this classical inverse problem to a central question in graph learning.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Forouhesh

item.title: Probe Sets for Nonlinear Kalman Filtering: Multi-Center Gains and Covariance Recalibration
item.description: arXiv:2609.14271v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kalman filters (KFs) choose the gain as the product of the state-measurement cross-covariance and the inverse of the innovation covariance. In nonlinear systems, the predictive distribution generally changes shape, and these covariances require approximation. Conventional nonlinear KFs approximate them around a single center, the predicted state. They can produce inaccurate gains and overconfident covariance estimates when one local approximation does not represent the measurement geometry across the uncertainty region. To address this issue, we introduce probe sets, small covariance-scaled collections of states at which the filter repeats its local approximation. We then select the gain that minimizes the average covariance reported by these local approximations. The same construction is used in our previously proposed covariance recalibration step to improve covariance consistency. The construction applies to different KF variants without requiring a specific approximation rule. For quadratic measurements, we derive conditions under which probing yields lower normalized true error variance than the corresponding single-center gain when prediction uncertainty is sufficiently understated. We apply the framework to four KF variants and compare the resulting filters with multiple baselines across 300 randomized setups for each of two systems. The results show that probing preserves typical accuracy while substantially reducing covariance inconsistency and the rare large-error trajectories that dominate the root mean square of per-run errors. The code is available at https://github.com/Shida-Jiang/Probe_KF.
